section_summary: The section closes a U.S. reply to Australian objections to the 1946–47 Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition, then records further exchanges about security, crews, observers, and whaling rules. A large intervening set of documents concerns a separate investigation into Joseph Goldstone and Howard H. MacGowan, who allegedly used an official small-business mission to arrange private cultured-pearl purchases in China and Japan. The section ends with Australia’s renewed request that Allied crews replace Japanese personnel.

subfiles.title: U.S. aide-mémoire replying to Australian objections to Japanese Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: The United States explains safeguards and the temporary character of the Japanese whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: The reply describes screening of Japanese personnel, limits on vessels approaching foreign land, advance disclosure of routes, and possible Australian security recommendations. It says future expeditions will involve prior Allied consultation and that permission to convert a tanker does not authorize its Antarctic use. The expedition is presented as an emergency food and fats measure that creates no future Japanese whaling right.

subfiles.title: Incoming Tokyo telegram concerning Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports on the proposed Japanese whaling expedition and related identification or inspection arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The telegram’s OCR is heavily damaged. Legible portions discuss a factory ship, Japanese tankers, identification markings or flags, and Fisheries Division recommendations concerning inspectors.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation concerning Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: A conversation addresses Japanese fishing vessels and the scope of whaling authorization.
subfiles.summary: Much of the text is illegible. The surviving passages concern whether fishing vessels and facilities remain subject to Allied decision and whether future activity requires prior consultation.

subfiles.title: Political Adviser despatch No. 626 forwarding personnel-screening check sheet
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a check sheet on screening the Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition’s personnel.
subfiles.summary: Forwards five copies of the September 17 security-screening check sheet.

subfiles.title: Check sheet on screening whaling-expedition personnel
subfiles.about: Requests intelligence screening of personnel on the 1946–47 Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Requests screening and identifies Hideo Ohmura as a source of vessel information.

subfiles.title: Attorney General’s letter on MacGowan and Goldstone
subfiles.about: Reports the Justice Department’s conclusion about MacGowan and Goldstone’s activities.
subfiles.summary: Finds no federal criminal-statute violation and returns the State Department file.

subfiles.title: Copy of Attorney General’s letter
subfiles.about: Duplicates the conclusion that no federal criminal violation was found.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the September 30 letter returning the Department’s file.

subfiles.title: State Department enclosure slip
subfiles.about: Records enclosure handling for the Attorney General correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Administrative enclosure slip referring to a letter addressed to the Attorney General.

subfiles.title: War Department memorandum on Joseph Goldstone’s confiscated pearls
subfiles.about: Explains why the Army proposes to return pearls seized from Joseph Goldstone in China.
subfiles.summary: The War Department says Goldstone is outside military jurisdiction and continued retention lacks legal justification. It proposes release to his Shanghai agent after he signs a liability release.

subfiles.title: Statement of Captain James L. King
subfiles.about: Describes Goldstone’s air ticket, baggage priority, and proposed business plans.
subfiles.summary: King says Goldstone obtained a 200-pound official baggage allowance, asked that its official designation and baggage description be erased from one copy, and discussed future pearl or jewelry business. Page 415 duplicates the statement’s second page.

subfiles.title: Criminal Investigation Division report on MacGowan and Goldstone
subfiles.from: John F. Stoskopf Jr. and George Plotkin
subfiles.to: Commanding General, United States Forces, China Theater
subfiles.about: Investigates private pearl trading during an ostensible U.S. Senate small-business mission.
subfiles.summary: The report reconstructs Goldstone and MacGowan’s travel to Shanghai and Tokyo, Goldstone’s purchases and attempted large-scale options on cultured pearls, and the seizure of pearls from his air baggage. It questions the authority and purpose of their official mission and alleges misuse of government transportation and prestige. It recommends wider notification, further investigation, confiscation of the pearls, and prosecution of any established crimes.

subfiles.title: Maverick telegram requesting investigation in Tokyo
subfiles.to: Commander in Chief, Allied Forces in the Pacific, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests investigation of MacGowan and Goldstone’s cultured-pearl dealings in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Maverick calls private transactions improper and orders MacGowan’s removal if involvement is established.

subfiles.title: Stoskopf telegram requesting Tokyo investigation
subfiles.about: Seeks evidence of MacGowan and Goldstone’s private cultured-pearl transactions.
subfiles.summary: Requests close observation and reports on their suspected attempt to corner the cultured-pearl market.

subfiles.title: Maverick telegram condemning private trade on government expense
subfiles.about: Urges action against Goldstone and MacGowan’s alleged private trading.
subfiles.summary: Maverick calls the conduct unethical, seeks MacGowan’s dismissal and both men’s return, and urges investigation of transportation misuse.

subfiles.title: China Theater Circular No. 48
subfiles.about: Restricts commercial use of government transportation and possession of goods.
subfiles.summary: States transport and goods restrictions cited in the seizure of Goldstone’s pearls.

subfiles.title: Notice concerning confiscated property
subfiles.doc_type: notice form, enclosure to exhibit D
subfiles.about: Provides a 60-day opportunity to request return of property seized under Circular No. 48.
subfiles.summary: Blank notice form explaining how to contest confiscation within 60 days.

subfiles.title: Goldstone Air Transport Command ticket
subfiles.about: Records Goldstone’s planned flight from Shanghai via Manila and baggage charges.
subfiles.summary: Ticket lists a 200-pound baggage allowance and $381.30 excess-baggage charge.

subfiles.title: Maverick letter authorizing investigation
subfiles.to: Commanding General, China Theater, Criminal Investigation Division
subfiles.about: Requests a full investigation of the Goldstone–MacGowan affair.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes investigation and accepts ship transport for MacGowan while it proceeds.

subfiles.title: Maverick telegram to Smaller War Plants Corporation
subfiles.to: Smaller War Plants Corporation, Washington, D.C.; information copy to Department of State
subfiles.about: Calls for MacGowan’s dismissal after Goldstone’s pearl shipment was discovered.
subfiles.summary: Maverick describes private trading during government travel as improper, asks that MacGowan’s employment and travel funding end, and urges notice to the Senate committee and federal authorities. He approves returning both men by ship.

subfiles.title: Sworn statement of Joe Goldstone
subfiles.about: Goldstone explains his Senate consultancy, travel, and pearl purchases.
subfiles.summary: Goldstone acknowledges buying about $20,000 of pearls for air shipment and another $8,500 for shipment by water. He says he paid his own travel expenses, MacGowan had no interest in the purchases, and he understood private business was permitted.

subfiles.title: Record of conference with MacGowan and Goldstone
subfiles.from: John F. Stoskopf Jr. and George Plotkin
subfiles.about: Records questioning of MacGowan and Goldstone about pearl transactions and their mission.
subfiles.summary: MacGowan acknowledges knowing about Goldstone’s purchases and attending negotiations but denies a personal interest. Both decline to answer some questions about prior plans or Goldstone’s funds. Goldstone affirms his written statement and says only the transactions it lists occurred.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of State Department telegram announcing small-business mission
subfiles.about: Announces Goldstone and MacGowan’s proposed mission and asks for travel information.
subfiles.summary: Lists proposed Chinese destinations and says the mission’s precise purpose will follow.

subfiles.title: Copy of Joe Goldstone’s calling card
subfiles.about: Shows the Senate Small Business Committee identification Goldstone used.
subfiles.summary: Card gives Goldstone’s Chicago address and Senate committee identification.

subfiles.title: Statement of Eve Lipkovsky
subfiles.about: Describes Goldstone’s prewar pearl dealings and renewed contacts before his Shanghai visit.
subfiles.summary: Says her family assembled pearls and Goldstone wanted continuing large shipments.

subfiles.title: Statement of Moses Lipkovsky
subfiles.about: Describes pearl sales and a proposed ongoing purchasing arrangement with Goldstone.
subfiles.summary: Lipkovsky says he assembled two shipments, one for Goldstone’s air baggage and one for shipment by water. He describes introducing Goldstone to Chase Bank’s manager and another major dealer; MacGowan attended many meetings.

subfiles.title: Statement of Boris Lipkovsky
subfiles.about: Describes preparing Goldstone’s pearl shipments and customs papers.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the air and water shipments and says MacGowan often accompanied Goldstone.

subfiles.title: Statement of Eric A. G. Petersen
subfiles.about: Describes Goldstone’s credit and proposed Chase Bank payments for pearls.
subfiles.summary: Reports two $50,000 credit letters and Goldstone’s proposed $100,000 purchasing deposit.

subfiles.title: Statement of Anatole Beerbrayer
subfiles.about: Describes Goldstone’s unsuccessful attempt to option Beerbrayer’s pearl stock.
subfiles.summary: Beerbrayer says Goldstone wanted to corner the pearl market and negotiated for roughly $400,000 of stock. The option expired after payment arrangements failed; MacGowan attended repeated meetings.

subfiles.title: Cathay Jewellery invoice No. 1066
subfiles.about: Itemizes cultured-pearl strands sold for Goldstone’s firm.
subfiles.summary: Records $20,008.50 in pearl strands and acknowledges payment.

subfiles.title: G. E. Marden customs-clearance invoice
subfiles.about: Charges for customs clearance of one case of pearls sent by air.
subfiles.summary: Itemizes export charges and payments in Chinese national currency.

subfiles.title: Shanghai Customs permit to ship pearls
subfiles.about: Permits shipment of a sealed box containing cultured pearls.
subfiles.summary: Lists 3,002 pearl strands for transport by airplane.

subfiles.title: Consular invoice for Goldstone’s cultured pearls
subfiles.about: Documents Goldstone’s pearl purchase and planned shipment as baggage.
subfiles.summary: Lists $20,008.50 in pearls plus export duty and air expenses.

subfiles.title: Goldstone–Beerbrayer pearl purchase option
subfiles.about: Sets terms for Goldstone’s proposed purchase of loose pearls and necklaces.
subfiles.summary: Option covers about 210,000 momme of pearls and 5,693 necklaces; expires December 10.

subfiles.title: Circular instruction forwarding Japanese fishing and whaling policy
subfiles.doc_type: circular instruction with routing and distribution sheets
subfiles.about: Distributes a press release reproducing U.S. policy conclusions on Japanese fisheries.
subfiles.summary: The instruction encloses Press Release No. 118 and its reproduction of SWNCC 99/3 conclusions on Japanese fisheries and aquatic industries. The distribution sheet lists posts in London, Ottawa, Oslo, Moscow, Canberra, and Wellington.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram requesting whaling rules and species-identification guides
subfiles.about: Requests regulatory and identification materials for observers on Japanese Antarctic whalers.
subfiles.summary: Requests copies of international whaling rules and illustrated whale-identification literature.

subfiles.title: State Department reply enclosing whaling agreements and identification guide
subfiles.about: Supplies whaling agreements and a whale-identification pamphlet.
subfiles.summary: Encloses six agreement sets and three identification guides, noting Remington Kellogg’s corrections.

subfiles.title: State Department letter enclosing instructions for whaling scientists and inspectors
subfiles.about: Sends guidance for biologists and inspectors accompanying whaling expeditions.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Kellogg’s instructions and stresses expert review of specimens and accurate whaling data.

subfiles.title: Urgent telegram asking about U.S. representatives on Japanese factory ships
subfiles.about: Asks whether U.S. factory-ship representatives received earlier instructions.
subfiles.summary: Requests an urgent reply on instructions to representatives aboard Japanese factory ships.

subfiles.title: Australian aide-mémoire requesting reconsideration of whaling crews
subfiles.about: Renews Australia’s objection to Japanese crews and possible precedent from the Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: Requests Allied crews, a clear statement that the expedition is not Japanese, and reconsideration of U.S. policy.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Australian ambassador on Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Records Australia’s request for Allied crews and the Acting Secretary’s response.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Makin warns that Japanese participation could support later claims to whaling rights and offers Allied crews. The Acting Secretary accepts the aide-mémoire, promises further consideration, and explains that the expedition serves emergency food and fats needs under continuing Allied authority.
